title: Comets: Dirty Snowballs
objective: After this level you can explain what comets are made of and why their tails point away from the Sun.
summary: Comets are icy “dirty snowballs.” Near the Sun they grow a coma and tails that always point away from it.

cards.headline: A comet’s tail can point ahead of it.
cards.body: Picture a comet and you probably see a tail streaming out behind it, like hair in the wind. Sometimes that tail is out in front. The comet doesn't get a vote: the Sun decides which way it points.

cards.headline: Dirty snowballs
cards.body: Comets are chunks of ice, dust and rock, often described as dirty snowballs. Many of the ones that return every few years are thought to come from the Kuiper Belt you met in Level 52. Far from the Sun, a comet is just that: a dirty snowball. As one nears the Sun, its ice turns to gas, forming a glowing cloud called a coma and long tails. A comet only puts on a show when it gets close enough for its ice to start turning to gas.

cards.headline: Tails that point away
cards.body: Sunlight and the solar wind push a comet's tails away from the Sun, always. So a tail isn't exhaust trailing behind the comet. It's more like a windsock, and the Sun is the wind. On the way in, the tail trails behind. On the way back out, it leads the way. Many comets actually have two tails: one of dust and one of charged gas.
cards.callout: Tails point away from the Sun

cards.fact: Halley's Comet returns about every 76 years.
cards.context: It last swung past Earth in 1986 and will be back in 2061. If you missed the last visit, 2061 is your next chance. Set a very long reminder.

questions.explanation: Comets are dirty snowballs of ice, dust and rock.

questions.prompt: Which way does a comet’s tail point?

options.label: Always behind the comet
options.rationale: As a comet leaves the Sun, its tail can lead.

questions.explanation: Sunlight and the solar wind push the tails away from the Sun, whatever direction the comet is moving.

questions.prompt: From Level 52: where are many comets that return every few years thought to come from?

options.label: The surface of the Sun
options.rationale: Comets come from the cold outer solar system.

questions.explanation: Many shorter-period comets come from the icy Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune.
